defs.def: to hit sb/sth hard or with force 撞；碰；撞击；碰撞

ex.s: For Japan, the   58   （number） are more striking -- 22 in 1950, 46 today and 53 in 2050.
These sculptures were painted a rainbow of striking colours.
ex.t: 这些雕塑被涂成了彩虹般鲜艳的各种颜色。

defs.def: to hit sb/sth with your hand or a weapon 打；击

ex.s: Because of this, Chinese literary works really strike a chord in the hearts of Egyptian readers.
ex.t: 因为这个原因,中国文学作品在埃及读者心中真的打响了和弦.

ex.s: "Three strikes and you are out" is another idiom that comes from baseball.
ex.t: "三击而你出局"是另一个来自于棒球的典型说法.

defs.def: to hit or kick a ball, etc. 击打，踢（球等）
to attack sb/sth, especially suddenly 突击；攻击
to happen suddenly and have a harmful or damaging effect on sb/sth 侵袭；爆发
to come into sb's mind suddenly 不用于进行时
to give sb a particular impression 给（某人以 … ）印象；让（某人）觉得

ex.s: They could have written pages on the necessity of computers, but writing, in and of itself, simply didn’t strike them as important.
ex.t: 他冲出希尔家，快速穿过街道。

defs.def: to fall on a surface 照在 … 上；照射
to put sb suddenly into a particular state 顿时使处于某状态
to refuse to work, because of a disagreement over pay or conditions 罢工
to rub sth such as a match against a surface so that it produces a flame; to produce a flame when rubbed against a rough surface 擦，划（火柴）；击出（火星）

ex.s: But Smith was struck mainly by the fact that she didn't truly grasp any of the skills the author described.
ex.t: 尽管史密斯确实拿到了最好的沙子，但用传统方式做事不仅仅是在玩弄法国泥巴。

defs.def: to show the time by making a ringing noise, etc. 敲；鸣；报时
to produce a musical note, sound, etc. by pressing a key or hitting sth 弹奏；奏响；发出（声音）
to discover gold, oil, etc. by digging or drilling 开采出；钻探到
to go somewhere with great energy or purpose 行进；加劲走
to try to hit sb/sth, especially with a weapon 朝 … 打去
to cause damage or have a serious effect on sb/sth 损害；有损于；严重影响到

ex.t: 他的评论让我感到奇怪。

ex.s: Tsunami waves can strike out of nowhere and cause a lot of destruction.
ex.t: 海啸波可以毫无征兆地袭来并造成巨大的破坏。

defs.def: to make sb unable to lead an active life; to make sb seriously ill; to kill sb 疾病等

ex.s: Struck by the doctor’s warning, I knew I had to make a change.
ex.t: 被医生的警告触动，我知道自己必须做出改变。

ex.s: Make a (3) to strike a balance between sport His latest (1) aren't good, and schoolwork.
ex.t: 做一个(3) 在运动之间取得平衡 他最新的(1)是不好的,和学校的工作。

defs.def: to hit sb very hard, so that they fall to the ground 击倒，撞倒（某人）
to start being independent 独立出去；自立谋生

ex.s: The French take their 35-hour workweek seriously — so seriously that some labor unions recently struck a deal with a group of companies limiting the number of hours that independent contractors can be on call.
ex.t: 法国人极其看重35小时工作周——以至于一些工会最近与一批公司达成协议，限制独立承包商待命的时长。

defs.def: to fail or be unsuccessful 失败；砸锅

ex.s: Few things strike fear into a child’s heart like the prospect of failing.
ex.t: 很少有东西像失败的预期那样能让孩子心里充满恐惧。

defs.def: to aim a sudden violent blow at sb/sth 挥拳猛击；猛打
to criticize sb/sth, especially in a public speech or in a book or newspaper （尤指公开）抨击
a period of time when an organized group of employees of a company stops working because of a disagreement over pay or conditions 罢工；罢课；罢市

ex.s: The similarity of moral virtues across cultures is striking, even though the relative ranking of the virtues may vary with a social group’s history and environment.
ex.t: 道德美德在各文化间的相似性令人惊叹，尽管这些美德的相对排序可能随社会群体的历史和环境而变化。

defs.def: a military attack, especially by aircraft dropping bombs 军事进攻；袭击；（尤指）空袭

ex.s: Hurricane Safety Guidelines Many people have no idea what to do when a disaster strikes.
ex.t: 飓风安全指南 很多人不知道灾难来临时该怎么做。

defs.def: an act of hitting or kicking sth/sb 击；打；踢
an unsuccessful attempt to hit the ball 击球未中；击
a situation in tenpin bowling when a player knocks down all the pins with the first ball 全中（第一球撞倒全部十柱球）
a sudden discovery of sth valuable, especially oil （珍贵东西的）意外发现；（尤指石油的）发现
a bad thing or action that damages sb/sth's reputation （有损声誉的）不利因素，打击
